candidates.tagline: You bought it to clean your floors. It was casing the joint.
candidates.story: SharkNinja robot vacuums stored your Wi-Fi password in plaintext and shared a single AWS certificate with 673,000 other devices — meaning anyone who unscrewed one vacuum could issue commands to all the others, download your home map, and tap into your camera feed.
candidates.why_funny: Your robot cleaner passed a more thorough security audit of your home than most IT departments would.
candidates.alt: A white Shark IQ robot vacuum sits on a hardwood floor looking completely innocent

candidates.tagline: SF café used AI food photos. Someone spray-painted 'SERIOUSLY.'
candidates.story: Grind & Unwind café in San Francisco used AI-generated images on their storefront menu that looked like food hallucinated by a model that had never seen food, sparking enough online fury that someone spray-painted 'SERIOUSLY' on the facade — costing the owner $700 to clean.
candidates.why_funny: The AI was given one job: make people want to eat here. It produced images that made people want to spray-paint the building.
candidates.alt: The Grind & Unwind café storefront with AI-generated food display photos visible in the window and graffiti on the facade
